# This fork's (2026-11-26, Retroid Pocket Nova, Adreno 740, docked): 788 of the game's 4,553 fragment shaders (every lit material) OR their light masks over the warp before the
# light loop: 5 butterfly shuffles when the warp is full, 10 indexed ones when it is not. Turnip's compiler turns each shuffle into a loop over the subgroup's lanes, so the main lit
# pass cost 6.5 ms of the frame's 12 whatever the resolution (27 draws, about 130,000 indices; depth test EQUAL after a pre-pass). As subgroups of one invocation the mask is the
# fragment's own and the shuffles are gone: the same pass 4.4 ms at 1600x900 where it took 6.5 at 1408x792
env
# As Link's Awakening (the same engine): the game waits for the frame before at each submission (acquire, SyncWait on the last frame's fence, submit, present), so a frame lasts the
# replay plus the GPU's time, the GPU idles while the frame is replayed, reads about 62% busy and its governor keeps it at 401 of 680 MHz: 14.2 ms of GPU at 1920x1080 and frames of
# 18.5 ms (about 45 dropped in 300) in Ganon's room. At its highest clock the same room takes 10.9-11.8 ms and 0-1 frames in 300 are dropped. The rate is held at 60: the frame work
# sits near the period, where the adaptive rate stepped down to 40 and back

# This fork's (2026-11-27, Retroid Pocket 6, 7.3 GB of RAM): the game was killed by lmkd ("device is not responding", 1.58 GB resident + 2.1 GB swapped) after
# graphics loaded slowly for minutes, and the device's VPN app was pushed out while it ran. The game's own heap is 3.1 GB; on top of it the host prepared every
# shader part of the bundle (9,858 shaders < the 30,000 default of DM_VK_GPL_PREP_MAX: all SPIR-V unpacked and 16,618 parts made at the start) and turned every
# memory pool into a hardware buffer up front (621 MB at the start). With the parts made when a program is first set (as Flight Simulator's 5000) and the pools
# made lazily in 32 MB chunks (as Luigi's Mansion 3's) the user played a dungeon without a kill
